thread.title: Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Google: Who Takes the Tech Crown in 2018?

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Google: Who Takes the Tech Crown in 2018?
text:
Shutterstock photo We are only about a week into 2018, but it's never too early to predict which tech giant will take this year's crown as the market’s top stock performer.
With all three major averages still logging all-time high closing levels, investors aren’t willing to let the decade-long bull market fizzle. This level of optimism, combined with corporate tax overhaul and the likelihood of cash repatriation, should propel equities higher. And this makes the FAANG stocks, given their hoards of cash overseas, even more compelling investments than they already were.
Of course, I’m referring to Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ). For good measure, we can include Microsoft ( MSFT ) in the mix. The company just ended its 2017 campaign with arguably one of the best stock performances (up 36% in 2017) it has had in its history. And that’s saying a lot, given that the tech giant was, at on point, the world’s most valuable company.
All told, these six technology behemoths crushed the market in 2017, posting average returns of 45%, compared with a 19% rise in the S&P 500 index. Take a look at the chart below.
With breathtaking returns to end the year, betting on these giants to duplicate their 2017 success would be a tough call. But given their strong brands and considerable market advantages, not having these stocks in any growth portfolio is just as risky. Just consider the ongoing battle taking place in high-growth markets like artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, the cloud, smart home and autonomous cars.
The competitive markets, not to mention the sustained growth in mobile devices, should continue to drive Apple, Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft higher. Google’s Waymo initiative gives it an early edge in autonomous vehicles over the likes of Tesla ( TSLA ), while Microsoft has built itself into a strong cloud company — one capable of challenging Amazon’s dominance with AWS.
Elsewhere, the strong growth in the ad market should continue to serve as tailwinds for Facebook and Google. The former is focusing on ways to drive higher engagements with videos and its new subscription platform, which in turn, can generate higher revenues. These initiatives are aimed making the ad business, which grew 47% in Q4 accounted for 99% of its overall revenue, more sustainable and profitable. Wall Street needs assurances Facebook has right strategies in place to fight off the emergence of Snap ( SNAP ). And the company delivered every quarter.
Netflix is another name to keep an eye on. After topping all of the FAANG names with 53% returns in 2017, the company has begun to see more competition not only for Hulu and Amazon, but also Disney ( DIS ), which just picked off some key assets from 21st Century Fox ( FOX ). Disney’s current ownership stake in Hulu now jumps to 60% by virtue of Fox’s own 30% stake. It remains to be seen whether Disney can execute in the manner it needs to rattle Netflix, but Netflix investors aren’t worried.
Not only are Netflix shares trading at all time highs to start the new year, the stock has already risen more than 10% to lead the group (FAANG+M). The good news is, with earnings season right around the corner and all six giants set to report in the next couple of weeks, investors won’t have to wait long to learn which tech stock will have the early performance lead and, thus, a potential edge for the rest of the year. But my money would be on all of them.
